sanskrit_shloka:
जनक उवाच ॥
अहो निरञ्जनः शान्तो बोधोऽहं प्रकृतेः परः ।
एतावन्तमहं कालं मोहेनैव विडम्बितः ॥ २-१॥
translation: Janaka said: Ah! I am truly the pure, stainless, peaceful Self, knowledge itself, beyond prakriti. For so long I have been deceived by ignorance and delusion.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Janaka said: Ah! I am truly the pure, stainless, peaceful Self, knowledge itself, beyond prakriti. For so long I have been deceived by ignorance and delusion.

commentary_faqs.question: Why does Janaka say 'Salutations to myself' (Namo Mahyam)?
commentary_faqs.answer: This is not an expression of ego, but a recognition of his true nature as the Supreme Brahman. He offers salutations to the infinite Consciousness that remains unchanged even when the universe is destroyed.

commentary_faqs.question: What is the significance of the 'ocean and waves' metaphor in this chapter?
commentary_faqs.answer: It illustrates that the universe and individual beings (waves) are not separate from the Self (the ocean). They arise from, exist in, and dissolve back into the same substance without ever being truly different from it.

commentary_faqs.question: How does Janaka define 'bondage' in Verse 22?
commentary_faqs.answer: Janaka realizes that his true bondage was not external circumstances, but the internal attachment to life and the mistaken identification with the individual soul (Jiva) instead of pure Consciousness.

sanskrit_shloka:

translation: Just as I alone illumine this body, so do I illumine the whole world. Therefore the entire world is mine; or else, truly, nothing exists at all.

commentary_faqs.question: How does Janaka define 'bondage' in Verse 22?
commentary_faqs.answer: Janaka realizes that his true bondage was not external circumstances, but the internal attachment to life and the mistaken identification with the individual soul (Jiva) instead of pure Consciousness.

sanskrit_shloka:
शरीरं स्वर्गनरकौ बन्धमोक्षौ भयं तथा ।
कल्पनामात्रमेवैतत् किं मे कार्यं चिदात्मनः ॥ २-२०॥
translation: The body, heaven and hell, bondage and liberation, and fear as well—this is mere imagination. What concern have they for me, the Self whose nature is Consciousness?

translations.author: English Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
अहो जनसमूहेऽपि न द्वैतं पश्यतो मम ।
अरण्यमिव संवृत्तं क्व रतिं करवाण्यहम् ॥ २-२१॥
translation: Ah, wondrous! Even in a crowd of people, I behold no duality. All has become to me like a silent forest; where, then, shall I seek enjoyment?

sanskrit_shloka:
नाहं देहो न मे देहो जीवो नाहमहं हि चित् ।
अयमेव हि मे बन्ध आसीद्या जीविते स्पृहा ॥ २-२२॥
translation: I am not the body, nor is the body mine. I am not the individual jīva; truly, I am pure Consciousness. This alone was my bondage: the craving for life.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहो भुवनकल्लोलैर्विचित्रैर्द्राक् समुत्थितम् ।
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ चित्तवाते समुद्यते ॥ २-२३॥
translation: Ah, wondrous! In me, the infinite great ocean, when the wind of the mind arises, the manifold waves of the world swiftly surge forth.

sanskrit_shloka:
मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधौ चित्तवाते प्रशाम्यति ।
अभाग्याज्जीववणिजो जगत्पोतो विनश्वरः ॥ २-२४॥
translation: In me, the infinite great ocean, when the wind of the mind subsides, the perishable boat of the world, steered by the merchant of life, the jīva, comes to ruin.

मय्यनन्तमहाम्भोधावाश्चर्यं जीववीचयः ।
